name: Missouri
summary_text: A visitor to Missouri stands under the national framework of the United States in every setting. Executive Order 14168 of January 2025 requires federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth, the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, and new passports are issued only as M or F, so a trans visitor's documents may not match their presentation. Airport screening and visa decisions follow the same national rules, including the State Department's February 2025 announcement that trans athletes seeking entry to compete in women's sporting events will be refused visas and flagged internally under the code 'SWS25', with a declaration of a gender other than sex assigned at birth capable of being treated as fraud and a permanent bar.  Missouri prohibits gender-affirming medical care for minors. The Save Adolescents from Experimentation (SAFE) Act, Senate Bill 49, took effect on 28 August 2023 after a St Louis judge denied a preliminary injunction against it on 29 August 2023. The statute bars hormones and puberty blockers for under-18s unless the patient was already in treatment, and prohibits all transition-related surgery for minors.  The SAFE Act also bars MO HealthNet Medicaid coverage of the prohibited care, restricts treatment access in prisons, jails and correctional centres, and exposes violating providers to licence revocation. CNN reports that the law additionally bars Missouri Medicaid from paying for gender-affirming care for a patient of any age, and that doctors who breach the ban can lose their state medical licence and be sued by patients up to 15 years after treatment.  Litigation over the ban has failed at every stage so far. Lambda Legal, the ACLU of Missouri and Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner filed suit on 25 July 2023 in Cole County Circuit Court on behalf of three families of transgender young people, medical providers, PFLAG National and GLMA, seeking to block Senate Bill 49 before its 28 August 2023 effective date. A Missouri judge upheld the law on 25 November 2024, and on 13 January 2026 the Missouri Supreme Court unanimously upheld the ban on gender-transition surgeries, cross-sex hormones and other gender-affirming care for minors, quoting the 2025 United States Supreme Court ruling that upheld Tennessee's similar ban. Counsel for the plaintiffs said they would appeal. The ban has been in force since 28 August 2023 and remains in force.  The statute carries a 2027 sunset enacted as a Republican-Democrat concession, but lawmakers have moved to make it permanent, and a November 2026 ballot initiative also seeks to ban such care indefinitely. The plaintiffs continue toward trial on the merits.  Correctional custody carries its own care exclusion. Governor Mike Kehoe signed an appropriations law, effective 2 July 2026, barring state funds from paying for cross-sex hormones or gender-transition surgery for transgender people in Missouri prisons, with no taper plan for inmates already receiving care. Missouri thereby became the seventh state, and the second in 2026 after Oklahoma, to ban gender-affirming care for inmates; Florida, Kentucky and North Carolina have near-identical laws, while similar Idaho and Georgia measures were blocked by federal courts.  A trans visitor to Missouri is unlikely to encounter the SAFE Act unless accompanying a minor who needs medical care, but anyone detained in a Missouri jail, prison or correctional centre loses access to state-funded hormone therapy and transition surgery under both the SAFE Act and the 2026 appropriations law.

name: Montana
summary_text: A trans visitor to Montana stands under the United States national travel-document regime. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas, and directed the attorney general to "correct the misapplication" of Bostock v. Clayton County (2020). The State Department stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth; new passport applications are processed only as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already issued with an X marker remain valid until they expire. In November 2025 the Supreme Court allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992. Travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at application, with some left stranded abroad. The ACLU has sued the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and Lambda Legal maintains guidance on what documentation to consider and how name and gender changes interact with federal records. A visitor's documents may therefore mismatch presentation at the border or at checkpoints. Screening carries an outing risk. TSA procedures can involve secondary screening, devices and pat-downs that are invasive of privacy. Several foreign governments responded: in April 2025 CNN reported that multiple countries issued advisories about trans people travelling to the United States over identity-document and data rules, and Axios reported in March 2025 that at least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the country. Montana's own legal position is unusually favourable relative to its statute book. The state has passed laws that would normally place it among the worst states for trans people, but Montana's courts have repeatedly blocked or enjoined those laws under the state constitution. Adult restrictions that were enacted have consequently not taken full effect, and that court record improved Montana's standing in the July 2026 anti-trans national legal risk assessment. Montana was the only state to improve in the 2026 rankings. The protections are judicial rather than statutory, so they depend on continued litigation. Nationally the youth-side picture remains unstable as federal policy shifts and litigation proceed. Executive Order 14187 (January 2025) described gender-affirming care for minors as "chemical and surgical mutilation of children," leading some hospitals to pause care; in summer 2025 the Department of Justice subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for full records of patients under 19, in July 2025 the federal government shut down specialised LGBTQ youth services on the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, and October 2025 proposed rules would bar Medicaid reimbursement for care to transgender patients under 18. Gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states. Several of these federal measures have been blocked or enjoined in court. Facilities access is restricted in a growing number of states. A Movement Advancement Project tally counts state bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings in nine states and one territory, with outright state bans on facility use per gender identity in additional states; 29 states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban, and some states make trans bathroom use a criminal offence in certain circumstances. In April 2025 a transgender student was arrested and handcuffed in a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol in what civil-rights attorneys described as the first known arrest under that state's bathroom-restriction law.

sources.documents: Codifies immutable male-female binary determined at birth; basis for state-level non-recognition of transgender status relevant to legal status and equal protection.

sources.title: Montana Senate Bill 99 (2023) - prohibition on gender-affirming care for trans minors
sources.documents: Most comprehensive state ban on gender-affirming care for minors; litigation history shows current enforceability and courts' view of discrimination and privacy rights.
sources.detail: Signed April 28, 2023 by Gov. Gianforte; preliminarily enjoined Sept 27, 2023 by District Judge Jason Marks citing Bostock v. Clayton County; injunction upheld Dec 11, 2024 by Montana Supreme Court with concurrence by Justice Laurie McKinnon on suspect class; permanently struck down May 14, 2025 by Judge Marks. ACLU of Montana and Lambda Legal filed suit. No URL visible.

sources.title: Montana birth certificate and driver's license gender-marker restrictions and injunctions
sources.documents: Documents ability of trans visitors/residents to update ID documents; enforcement status of bans on changes absent data-entry error, DNA test, or surgery/court order.
sources.detail: Sept 9, 2022 DPHHS rule banning updates, blocked Sept 15, 2022; Feb 22, 2023 bill prohibiting changes on all IDs signed May 19, 2023; enjoined Dec 2024 by District Judge Mike Menahan; preliminary block Dec 16, 2024 extended to trial citing sex discrimination; upheld April 15, 2026 by Montana Supreme Court, Justice Laurie McKinnon on dignity. Prior rules: surgery required until Dec 2017, then affidavit + Gender Designation Form + court order; April 2021 surgical-procedure requirement blocked April 2022 for vagueness, followed by May 2022 emergency rule. ACLU sued July 2021. No URL visible.

sources.title: Montana House Bill 121 (2025) - sex-segregated bathrooms, locker rooms, sleeping areas in publicly-funded facilities
sources.documents: Direct safety/access risk for trans visitors using public facilities; shows enforcement attempt and judicial check.
sources.detail: Passed Feb 2025; ACLU of Montana sued; temporary restraining order April 2, 2025 by District Court Judge Shane Vannatta ruling bill 'motivated by animus' with no evidence advancing women's safety/privacy. sources.title: Montana House Bill 359 (2023) - restriction on sexually oriented/obscene performances and drag story hours
sources.documents: Criminalization risk around drag/trans expression in public spaces where minors may be present and in publicly-funded schools/libraries.
sources.detail: Passed May 2023 along party lines; led to cancellation of Butte-Silver Bow library reading by transgender woman; temporarily restrained July 2023 prior to Big Sky Pride by District Court Judge Brian Morris as 'vague and overbroad' with risk of disproportionate enforcement against trans, Two-Spirit, gender nonconforming people; extended Oct 2024. Follow-on HB 675 defeated March 2025 with 13 Republicans joining Democrats. No URL visible.

sources.title: Montana House Bill 819 (May 2025) - government flag 'neutrality' law
sources.documents: Prohibits official display of flags representing sexual orientation, gender, political ideology; interpreted to ban Pride flags by governments/schools; Missoula rainbow-flag municipal-flag workaround.
sources.detail: Defines flag as physical/digital installation on flagpole, building, wall, vehicle, structure; exempts governmental, territorial, school, historical (e.g., Gadsden), law enforcement flags. No URL visible.
